newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani rupee ends up in kerb, seen falling.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani rupee ends up in kerb, seen falling.

text.p: The Pakistani rupee closed 0.01 up at 41.32 to the dollar on Tuesday, but dealers said it was likely to open down on Wednesday amid rising demand for the U.S. currency.
They said a volatile stock market and low gold prices were expected to prompt investors to buy dollars as a safe haven.

The State (central) Bank of Pakistan rate, changed on July 11, was 40.5200/40.7226 against the dollar. The premium on foreign exchange bearer certificates closed at 2.0 percent, from its previous close at 2.20 percent.
